stops.note: possibly meaning "to smear" or "to sketch quickly"
applied to cheap, sentimental, mass-produced art
Munich art dealers used it in the 1860s–70s for cheap sketches; Clement Greenberg's 1939 essay spread it in English
stops.meaning: art or objects considered tacky or overly sentimental

current_meaning: art, objects, or design considered tacky, garish, or overly sentimental
